source_steps.text: Fix z0∈Z and assume L1: z0∈Ω. The set Ω is open, since positivity is an open condition on the continuous time projection. H001 and the definition of Uext give C∞ regularity on Ω: locally this is exactly the original jointly smooth map, and no value at nonpositive times is used. E004 gives differentiability of Uext there and C∞ regularity of its derivative map. For a constant direction, its constant vector field has zero derivative and all higher derivatives zero; E005 therefore makes evaluation of that derivative map in the direction C∞. Induction repeats E004 and E005 for every finite ordered constant-direction derivative. In particular Uext,u_t,u_j,u_tt,u_jj have the required derivatives at every positive-time point. For the affine time curve r↦(x,r), the derivative is τ; for the affine spatial curve h↦(x+h ε_j,r), it is σ(j). Their linear remainders are identically zero. E013 applied to Uext, and then to its derivative fields, identifies the directional fields with the ordinary partial derivatives in H001. The curves stay in Ω near each point under consideration. These assertions hold at every point of Ω and for every spatial index.

At z0, apply E008 with both factors Uext and direction τ. Real inner-product symmetry and ⟪v,v⟫=‖v‖² give D_τ(⟪Uext,Uext⟫)(z0)=2⟪Uext(z0),u_t(z0)⟫. H002 says ⟪Uext,Uext⟫=1 on the open set Ω. Hence the scalar field agrees with the constant 1 on a neighborhood of z0; E010 identifies its Fréchet derivative with the zero derivative of that constant. Dividing by 2 yields tangency ⟪Uext(z0),u_t(z0)⟫=0.

The acceleration clause of H002 at the positive-time point z0, using the partial-derivative identifications F001 and Δ_xu=Σ_j u_jj, gives a real scalar witness for u_tt(z0)−Δ_xu(z0)=a Uext(z0). Record existence before selecting that witness.

Choose the witness a0 from F003. Taking its inner product with u_t(z0), bilinearity and symmetry give ⟪u_t(z0),u_tt(z0)−Δ_xu(z0)⟫=a0⟪u_t(z0),Uext(z0)⟫=0 by F002. This conclusion does not depend on the private choice of a0, so existential elimination removes that witness. No scalar field has been selected and no derivative of a scalar witness has been taken.

Combine F002 and F004, discharge L1 into the condition z0∈Ω, and universally quantify z0. Since Ω is precisely the set of all spatial points and positive times, and F001 identifies every derivative with the original partial derivative, these are both identities of the exported conclusion for every x and t>0, with no scalar regularity assumption.

The set Ω is open: it is the inverse image of (0,∞) under the continuous time projection. H001 implies Uext is C∞ on Ω, since it agrees there locally with the original smooth map. E004 supplies differentiability and a smooth derivative map. Evaluate it at any constant direction with E005; constant fields are smooth because their derivatives and all higher derivatives vanish. This makes the directional derivative smooth. Induction repeats these two operations: every finite ordered constant-direction derivative of Uext is C∞ on Ω and differentiable there. At interior points differentiability on the open set is ordinary differentiability. In particular all fields u_t,u_j,u_tt,u_jj,u_tj are smooth. This argument makes no assertion outside Ω.

Apply E009 to each pair defining T,A_j,B_j,H_j and to the repeated factors u_t,u_t and u_j,u_j. The identity ⟪v,v⟫=‖v‖² identifies the latter scalar fields with the squared norms. E014 sums the finite family consisting of the time square and the n spatial squares, giving smoothness of e with precisely its stated normalization. Apply E004 to this scalar e and E005 to its derivative map and the constant τ to obtain smoothness of e_t=Ddir(τ,e). Thus every scalar field in the exported conclusion is jointly smooth on Ω, as are the vector derivative fields already established.

For every z∈Ω and fixed constant directions v,w∈Z, apply E007 to the derivative map of Uext and the constant field with value v. The derivative of that constant field is zero, so evaluating the resulting equality in w gives D_w(D_v Uext)(z)=(fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ Uext) z)(w)(v). The derivative map is differentiable by F001 and E004, since it is smooth on the open Ω. Smoothness also gives C² regularity at z. E006 therefore interchanges w and v in the second Fréchet derivative, yielding D_wD_v Uext(z)=D_vD_w Uext(z). Taking v=σ(j) and w=τ for each j proves Ddir(τ,u_j(j))=u_tj(j) throughout Ω. This is a proved mixed-direction identity, rather than a property of the notation.

Fix arbitrary t0 and assume L1: t0>0. Then 0<t0/2<3t0/2, and H003 applied to these endpoints gives existence of a compact spatial set on whose complement u=q throughout [t0/2,3t0/2]. Record this existence before choosing a set.

Choose C0 from F004 and define O0=(X∖C0)×(t0/2,3t0/2). A compact subset of Euclidean space is closed and Borel measurable; hence O0 is open. The interval in this product is contained in (0,∞), so O0⊂Ω, and Uext=q on O0 by the choice of C0. These are the only properties of C0 used: no boundary smoothness or nonempty interior is required.

At every point of O0, E010 compares Uext with the constant q on an open neighborhood, giving zero derivative. Inductively, if an ordered positive-order derivative field is identically zero on O0, E010 makes its derivative zero there as well. This proves vanishing of every positive-order derivative of Uext on O0. The same locality argument compares e with zero on O0: e vanishes there because its vector factors vanish, so e_t vanishes there too. Each of T,A_j,B_j,H_j vanishes by its defining inner product. Thus a single C0 supports all these fields for every time in the open slab.

E019 applies with source set all of X and target set Ω: the inclusion has constant derivative and higher derivatives zero, and maps into Ω because r>0. Thus all spatial sections are smooth, in particular continuous. Likewise restriction along r↦(x,r) and E013 identify their time partials with the directional derivatives; E013 on the affine spatial coordinate curves identifies their spatial partials. These affine curves have their indicated constant derivatives with zero remainder. This proves agreement with the original ordinary derivatives in the exported conclusion, including ∂_t e=e_t and, using F003, ∂_t u_j=∂_{x_j}u_t. For times in the chosen open slab, F006 shows that each positive-order derivative section and each listed scalar section has topological support contained in the closed compact C0. The section of Uext itself is smooth; its value outside C0 is q, and no compact-support claim about Uext is made.

E003 makes its restriction to compact C0 integrable. E012 then makes its C0 indicator integrable on X, and that indicator equals the original section pointwise by F006. This proves integrability of all the scalar products, including the undifferentiated H_j. The same argument applied to the norm of any vector derivative section proves integrability of that norm: the norm is continuous and vanishes off C0. The vector section itself is continuous into a finite-dimensional real normed space, hence strongly measurable; integrability of its norm is precisely the remaining condition for Bochner integrability. This also covers any finite-order derivative field, with its finite-dimensional derivative-tensor codomain. Thus every section meant by the exported conclusion is integrable. The reasoning still applies to an empty C0, when all sections vanish.

import Mathlib
open MeasureTheory Set Filter
open scoped Topology ContDiff BigOperators

namespace WaveEnergy
abbrev X (n : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
abbrev V (m : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)
abbrev Z (n : ℕ) := X n × ℝ
def omega (n : ℕ) : Set (Z n) := {z | 0 < z.2}
def tau (n : ℕ) : Z n := (0, 1)
noncomputable def basis (n : ℕ) (j : Fin n) : X n := EuclideanSpace.single j 1
noncomputable def sigma (n : ℕ) (j : Fin n) : Z n := (basis n j, 0)
noncomputable def D {n : ℕ} {F : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    (v : Z n) (f : Z n → F) (z : Z n) : F := fderiv ℝ f z v
noncomputable def ordered {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) : List (Z n) → Z n → V m
  | [] => U
  | v :: vs => D v (ordered U vs)
noncomputable def ut {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) := D (tau n) U
noncomputable def uj {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) (j : Fin n) := D (sigma n j) U
noncomputable def utt {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) := D (tau n) (ut U)
noncomputable def ujj {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) (j : Fin n) := D (sigma n j) (uj U j)
noncomputable def utj {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) (j : Fin n) := D (sigma n j) (ut U)
noncomputable def lap {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) (z : Z n) := ∑ j, ujj U j z
noncomputable def density {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) (z : Z n) : ℝ :=
  ‖ut U z‖ ^ 2 + ∑ j, ‖uj U j z‖ ^ 2
noncomputable def energy {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x, density U (x, t)
noncomputable def timeProd {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) (z : Z n) : ℝ :=
  inner ℝ (ut U z) (utt U z)
noncomputable def gradProd {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) (j : Fin n) (z : Z n) : ℝ :=
  inner ℝ (uj U j z) (utj U j z)
noncomputable def lapProd {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) (j : Fin n) (z : Z n) : ℝ :=
  inner ℝ (ut U z) (ujj U j z)
noncomputable def flux {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) (j : Fin n) (z : Z n) : ℝ :=
  inner ℝ (ut U z) (uj U j z)
noncomputable def densityTime {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) := D (tau n) (density U)
noncomputable def rate {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) (z : Z n) : ℝ :=
  2 * timeProd U z + 2 * ∑ j, gradProd U j z
def ScalarField {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) (f : Z n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  f = density U ∨ f = densityTime U ∨ f = timeProd U ∨
    ∃ j, f = gradProd U j ∨ f = lapProd U j ∨ f = flux U j
def SectionFacts {n : ℕ} {F : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup F]
    (f : Z n → F) (C : Set (X n)) (r : ℝ) : Prop :=
  Continuous (fun x => f (x, r)) ∧
  tsupport (fun x => f (x, r)) ⊆ C ∧
  HasCompactSupport (fun x => f (x, r)) ∧
  Integrable (fun x => f (x, r)) volume
def Regular {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) : Prop :=
  (∀ ds, ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (ordered U ds) (omega n)) ∧
  (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (iteratedFDeriv ℝ k U) (omega n)) ∧
  (∀ f, ScalarField U f → ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ f (omega n))
def Localized {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) (C : Set (X n)) (r : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ ds, ds ≠ [] →
    (∀ x, x ∉ C → ordered U ds (x, r) = 0) ∧ SectionFacts (ordered U ds) C r) ∧
  (∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k →
    (∀ x, x ∉ C → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k U (x, r) = 0) ∧
      SectionFacts (iteratedFDeriv ℝ k U) C r) ∧
  (∀ f, ScalarField U f →
    (∀ x, x ∉ C → f (x, r) = 0) ∧ SectionFacts f C r)
def LocalData {n m : ℕ} (U : Z n → V m) : Prop :=
  ∀ t₀ : ℝ, 0 < t₀ → ∃ C : Set (X n), IsCompact C ∧
    ∀ r ∈ Ioo (t₀ / 2) (3 * t₀ / 2), Localized U C r
end WaveEnergy
open WaveEnergy

conclusion.statement:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
